## Proof

**Claim.** The VC-dimension of $H_{N\text{-parity}}$ is $N$.

**Lower bound: $\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{N\text{-parity}}) \ge N$.**

Consider the $N$ standard basis vectors $e_1, \dots, e_N \in \{0,1\}^N$, where $e_j$ has a $1$ in coordinate $j$ and $0$ elsewhere. Let $\ell : \{e_1,\dots,e_N\} \to \{0,1\}$ be an arbitrary labeling. We must find $I \subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$ with $h_I(e_j) = \ell(j)$ for every $j$.

Now $h_I(e_j) = \big(\sum_{i \in I} (e_j)_i\big) \bmod 2 = \mathbf{1}[j \in I]$. Hence $h_I(e_j) = \ell(j)$ iff ($j \in I \iff \ell(j)=1$). Setting $I = \{j : \ell(j) = 1\}$ realizes the labeling. So $\{e_1,\dots,e_N\}$ is shattered, giving $\mathrm{VCdim} \ge N$.

**Upper bound: $\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{N\text{-parity}}) \le N$.**

Take any $N+1$ points $x_1, \dots, x_{N+1} \in \{0,1\}^N$, viewed as vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^N$. Since $\dim_{\mathbb{F}_2} \mathbb{F}_2^N = N < N+1$, these vectors are linearly dependent: there is a nonempty set $S \subseteq \{1,\dots,N+1\}$ with
$$\sum_{j \in S} x_j = \mathbf{0} \pmod 2.$$

For every $I \subseteq \{1,\dots,N\}$, the labels $h_I(x_j)$ satisfy
$$\sum_{j \in S} h_I(x_j) = \sum_{j \in S}\Big(\sum_{i \in I} (x_j)_i\Big) = \sum_{i \in I}\Big(\sum_{j \in S}(x_j)_i\Big) = \sum_{i \in I} 0 = 0 \pmod 2.$$

So the labels on the points indexed by $S$ always have **even parity**. Now consider the labeling that assigns $1$ to exactly one point of $S$ and $0$ to every other point (in particular to all remaining points of $S$). The sum of labels over $S$ equals $1$, which is odd — contradicting the even-parity constraint. Hence this labeling is not realizable by any $h_I$, so $\{x_1,\dots,x_{N+1}\}$ is not shattered.

Since no $N+1$ points are shattered, $\mathrm{VCdim} \le N$.

**Conclusion.** Combining both bounds, $\mathrm{VCdim}(H_{N\text{-parity}}) = N$.
